title: Losing It
structure: typical: drum-and-bass-driven intro over two 16-bar phrases with the 'losing it' vocal stab teasing in, rising build into a stripped drop where the kick and rolling bassline carry the track; second breakdown/build mid-track; percussive outro phrase for the mix-out.

title: Flash
structure: typical: dry drum-machine intro phrases before the acid bassline and the spoken 'cameras ready, prepare to flash' vocal enter; hypnotic loop-based arrangement with vocal phrases dropping in and out rather than a defined breakdown; long percussive outro.

title: One More Time
structure: typical: filtered sample hook opens immediately with the kick (short intro, so cue-in on the first downbeat), Romanthony vocal verses over 16-bar phrases, long filtered breakdown with the vocal alone in the middle third, full hook returns, extended fade-style outro. Practise phrase counting through the breakdown.

artist: Armand Van Helden feat. Duane Harden
title: U Don't Know Me
structure: typical: string-stab and drum intro phrases before the disco-sample bassline and Duane Harden vocal enter; verse/hook structure in 16-bar phrases with a strings-led breakdown mid-track; percussive outro for blending out.

title: Music Sounds Better With You
structure: typical: filtered guitar-loop intro over the kick for the first phrases, the single repeating vocal line enters and the arrangement is built from the filter opening and closing over that loop; long filtered breakdown then full hook, then a long loop-based outro.

title: Pjanoo
structure: typical: drum-and-bass intro phrases before the piano riff enters, the riff is teased under a filter then fully released after a breakdown; second breakdown/build mid-track; long beat-only outro. Good for hearing a semitone shift on the piano hook.

title: Hey Hey
structure: typical: percussion-and-bass intro phrases, the 'hey hey' vocal hook and organ stabs enter on a phrase boundary, vocal breakdown mid-track then full groove; stripped percussive outro.

title: Need U (100%)
structure: typical: drum intro with chopped vocal fragments, the organ bass and full A*M*E vocal enter after the first phrases; sung breakdown mid-track leading into the main hook; beat-only outro.

title: White Noise
structure: typical: synth-bass and drum intro phrases, Aluna vocal verses in 16-bar phrases, defined 'white noise' hook, breakdown mid-track then hook; outro shortens quickly so mix out on the last hook phrase.

title: Latch
structure: typical: short instrumental intro, Sam Smith verses and a strongly defined chorus hook in 16-bar phrases, sung breakdown before the final chorus; short outro. Melodic content makes key changes obvious.

title: Turn Off The Lights
structure: typical: extended drum intro phrases, the spoken 'turn off the lights' vocal enters on a phrase boundary and the bass drop follows a short build; vocal breakdown mid-track then second drop; percussive outro for the blend-out.

title: (It Goes Like) Nanana
structure: typical: 6:07 original mix; drum and bass intro phrases, the piano riff and 'nanana' vocal hook enter after the intro phrases, breakdown mid-track then hook; long groove-based outro for the mix-out.

title: Glue
structure: typical: breakbeat-style drums and pad intro, the vocal-sample hook and synth line build over successive phrases rather than a single drop; sustained pads make the filter very audible; long pad-and-drum outro.

title: Cola
structure: typical: 6:55 original mix; long drum-and-bass intro phrases, Elderbrook vocal enters on a phrase boundary, spoken 'she drinks coca-cola' hook, sung breakdown mid-track then groove; extended percussive outro.

title: Take It
structure: typical: 5:46 extended mix; percussive intro phrases, spoken 'take it' vocal stab and rolling bassline drop in after the intro, breakdown and second drop mid-track; beat-only outro.

title: Where You Are
structure: typical: short intro, Hayla verse over a bassline, big sung build into a synth-led drop, second verse/build/drop; outro is short so mix out during the last drop phrase.

title: Good Life
structure: typical: drum-machine and bass intro phrases, Paris Grey vocal verses and the 'good life' chorus hook, instrumental breakdown mid-track then chorus; long beat outro on the 12" version.

title: Show Me Love
structure: typical: the M1 organ bass and drums open the track, Robin S verses and the 'show me love' chorus in 16-bar phrases, breakdown mid-track then chorus; organ-and-drum outro. Dominant bassline is ideal for bass-swap practice.

title: Ready For Your Love
structure: typical: 4:52 extended mix; drum-and-bass intro phrase, MNEK verses with a defined sung chorus hook, breakdown then chorus; short beat outro.

title: Home
structure: typical: 6:41 club mix; drum and bass intro phrases, the melodic synth theme and vocal enter after the intro, a long pad-led breakdown mid-track and a restrained return; extended melodic outro.

title: Brightest Lights
structure: typical: 6:52 original mix; long pad-and-drum intro phrases, Poliça vocal enters on a phrase boundary, a sustained melodic breakdown mid-track, gradual layered return; long pad outro that reacts well to filter sweeps.

title: Gravity
structure: typical: 9:24 original mix; long minimal drum intro phrases, Laura Korinth vocal and the lead synth enter after the intro, extended breakdown mid-track before the main melodic section; very long stripped outro for slow blends.

title: Your Mind
structure: typical: 8:22 original mix; long percussive intro phrases, the 'your mind' vocal sample and rolling bassline build across phrases, sustained breakdown with the vocal alone mid-track then the full groove; long beat outro.

title: Forget
structure: typical: drum-and-bass intro phrases, vocal sample and bassline hook enter on a phrase boundary, breakdown mid-track then groove; long percussive outro.

title: Buggin'
structure: typical: 8:25 original mix; long drum-and-bass intro phrases, Jem Cooke vocal enters after the intro, sung breakdown mid-track then groove; long stripped outro for extended blends.
typical: drum intro phrases, chopped vocal hook and piano chords enter on a phrase boundary, sung breakdown mid-track then hook; beat-only outro on the extended mix.

title: My Love
structure: typical: 4:19 original; short drum intro, deep bassline and Jess Glynne verses, defined sung chorus, breakdown mid-track then chorus; short outro so mix out on the final chorus phrase.

title: Where's Your Head At
structure: typical: 4:45 original; the sampled synth riff and vocal hook open almost immediately, verse/hook structure in 16-bar phrases, breakdown mid-track then hook; short outro. High-energy hook suits echo-out practice.

title: Around The World
structure: typical: bassline and drum intro phrases with the vocoder hook entering on a phrase boundary, elements are added and removed in 16-bar blocks rather than a single breakdown, long bass-and-drum outro. Dominant bassline is ideal for bass-swap and loop practice.

title: Opus
structure: typical: 9:03 original mix built as one long crescendo: sparse drum-and-synth intro phrases, the arpeggio motif thickens phrase by phrase into a sustained build that peaks late in the track, followed by a long stripped outro. Practise phrase counting through a very long build.

title: Doppler
structure: Drum/percussion intro for two 16-bar phrases; the signature Doppler-style pitch-riser is the hook and builds across a full phrase into the drop; a mid-track breakdown strips to the riser before the second drop; long stripped outro. typical: use the first two phrases for blend-in.

title: Sgadi Li Mi
structure: typical: kick/percussion intro for two 16-bar phrases, chanted vocal hook enters on the third phrase, breakdown drops the kick under the vocal then rebuilds, second peak section, long drum outro.

title: Higher
structure: typical: driving drum intro for two 16-bar phrases, 'higher' vocal stab and lead ride enter on the third phrase, breakdown pulls the kick and holds the vocal before a snare-roll build into the second drop, extended drum outro.

title: The Bells
structure: Loop-based classic with no conventional breakdown: drums open, the bell-stab riff enters within the first phrases and runs almost throughout; elements drop in and out on 16-bar boundaries. typical: treat every phrase boundary as a mix point; short track so plan the blend early.

title: Born Slippy (Nuxx)
structure: Opens beatless on the synth chord stabs and 'drive boy dog boy' vocal for the first phrases before the kick enters; long beat section with vocal phrases; the beat drops out again mid-track before returning; extended outro. typical: cue from the kick entry rather than the beatless intro.

title: Move Your Body To The Beat
structure: typical: kick-and-acid intro for two 16-bar phrases, 'move your body to the beat' vocal enters on the third phrase, breakdown holds the vocal and acid line without kick then rebuilds, second peak, drum outro.

title: The Age Of Love
mix: Charlotte de Witte & Enrico Sangiuliano Remix
structure: typical: drum intro for two 16-bar phrases, the classic arpeggio riff enters on the third phrase, long breakdown strips to the riff and pads with a sustained riser build, drop back to full kick, extended drum outro.

title: Moon Rocks
structure: typical: long percussive intro across two 16-bar phrases, rolling bass groove and lead motif build in phrase by phrase, breakdown mid-track with a slow riser, second drop, long stripped outro. Tempo is below the 128 floor; use it for slow-techno blends.

title: Insomnia
structure: Long DJ intro before the first vocal; Maxi Jazz spoken verses over the groove; the famous lead-synth riff is withheld until after the breakdown roughly midway, then rides to the end; extended outro. typical: count the intro in 16-bar phrases and cue the riff entry as the main drop.

title: Sandstorm
structure: The stabbing lead riff is present from the first phrase with the drums; breakdown mid-track drops the kick and rebuilds with the riff and snare roll; second drop; outro thins to riff and drums. typical: use the last two phrases for blend-out. Note: Tunebat lists this entry as B minor (10A) and an 'Original Version' entry as E minor (9A).

title: Communication
structure: typical: beat intro for two 16-bar phrases, bass and arpeggio enter on the third phrase, long breakdown with the lead melody and pads, snare-roll build into the main drop, extended drum outro.

title: Sun & Moon
structure: typical: drum intro for two 16-bar phrases, chords enter on the third phrase, Richard Bedford vocal verse, breakdown with the vocal chorus over pads, riser build into the drop, second vocal section, long drum outro.

title: For An Angel
structure: typical: drum intro for two 16-bar phrases, bassline on the third, the arpeggiated lead melody enters a phrase later, long mid-track breakdown holding the melody over pads, snare build into the drop, extended outro.

title: Adagio For Strings
structure: typical: drum intro for two 16-bar phrases, the Barber string theme enters and builds phrase by phrase, long central breakdown with the strings alone, extended riser and snare build into the drop, long outro.

title: No Problem
structure: typical: vocal-sample intro over sparse drums for two 16-bar phrases, build on the second phrase, first drop lands at bar 33 (start of the third phrase), mid-track breakdown, second drop, short outro.

title: Tarantula
structure: typical: ragga vocal intro (Tenor Fly / MC Spyda) over intro drums for two 16-bar phrases, first drop at the third phrase (bar 33) with the reese bass, breakdown with vocal, second drop, drum outro.

title: Rock It
structure: typical: melodic intro for two 16-bar phrases with the vocal cut, riser build across the second phrase, first drop on the third phrase (bar 33), breakdown, second drop, short outro.

title: Afterglow
structure: typical: piano and Becky Hill vocal intro for two 16-bar phrases, drums fill in on the second phrase, first drop at the third phrase (bar 33), vocal breakdown mid-track, second drop, short outro. Tunebat's solo-artist entry lists the half-time 87 BPM value.

title: Heartbeat Loud
structure: typical: vocal and pad intro for two 16-bar phrases, riser build on the second, first drop at bar 33, breakdown with the Fiora vocal, second drop, drum outro.

title: Desire
structure: typical: vocal and synth intro for two 16-bar phrases, snare build, first drop at the third phrase (bar 33), breakdown on the vocal hook, second drop, short outro (short 3:35 edit so phrases are tight).

title: Scary Monsters and Nice Sprites
structure: Melodic synth intro with the 'oh my gosh' vocal cut, build, then the first drop lands after the intro phrases; a melodic breakdown returns before the second drop; short outro. typical: first drop at the start of the third 16-bar phrase.

title: I Can't Stop
structure: typical: synth-chord intro for two 16-bar phrases with the 'I can't stop' vocal, snare build, first drop at the third phrase (bar 33), breakdown on the chords, second drop, short outro.

title: Woo Boost
structure: typical: 'woo' vocal-sample intro over sparse drums for two 16-bar phrases, first drop with the wobble bass on the third phrase (bar 33), breakdown, second drop, drum outro.

title: Promises
structure: typical: Alana Watson vocal intro over pads for two 16-bar phrases, snare build on the second, first drop at the third phrase (bar 33), vocal breakdown, second drop, short outro. (Nero's original is listed at 72 BPM half-time, so the remix is the DJ version.)

title: Animals
structure: typical: drum intro for two 16-bar phrases, the plucked lead motif enters on the third phrase, breakdown with the melody alone and a long snare/riser build, big-room drop, second breakdown and drop, drum outro.

artist: Swedish House Mafia feat. John Martin
title: Don't You Worry Child
structure: typical: drum intro for two 16-bar phrases, piano chords and John Martin verse enter on the third phrase, chorus breakdown with the vocal over pads, riser build into the drop, second verse/chorus/drop, drum outro.

title: Spaceman
structure: typical: drum intro for two 16-bar phrases, lead enters on the third phrase, breakdown with the melodic hook and long snare build, big-room drop, second breakdown/drop, drum outro.

title: Levels
structure: typical: drum intro for two 16-bar phrases, the piano riff enters on the third phrase, breakdown on the Etta James vocal sample, riser build into the drop, second breakdown and drop, drum outro.

title: Clarity
structure: typical: piano and Foxes vocal intro, verse, sung chorus build into the synth drop, second verse and drop, short outro. Vocal-led, so cue from the first downbeat of the verse.

title: Where Are Ü Now
structure: typical: piano and vocal intro for two 16-bar phrases, the pitched 'dolphin' vocal hook is the drop on the third phrase, vocal breakdown, second drop, short outro.

title: Rio
structure: typical: vocal intro over pads for two 16-bar phrases, snare build, first drop at the third phrase (bar 33), vocal breakdown, second drop, short outro.

title: Hold Your Colour
structure: typical: melodic intro for two 16-bar phrases, riser build, first drop at the third phrase (bar 33), long melodic breakdown, second drop, drum outro. Tunebat lists the half-time 87 BPM value.

title: Dance With Me
structure: typical: drum and bass intro for two 16-bar phrases, the lead synth motif enters on the third phrase, long melodic breakdown mid-track with a riser, drop back to the groove, long stripped outro.

title: Hidden Beauties
structure: typical: hypnotic drum intro for two 16-bar phrases, the pad theme and bassline enter on the third phrase, a long breakdown mid-track with a slow riser, return to the groove, long outro.

title: Astral Projection
structure: typical: percussive intro across two 16-bar phrases, the lead motif builds in phrase by phrase, long central breakdown with a riser, drop, extended stripped outro.

title: Still D.R.E.
structure: typical: the Scott Storch piano stab loops from bar 1 with no lead-in, drums enter after the first phrase, hook is Snoop's 'Still D.R.E.' refrain every 16 bars; the isolated piano stab is the standard hot-cue hit.

title: Made You Look
structure: typical: built on the Incredible Bongo Band 'Apache' break, so the drum-only intro doubles as a scratchable break; 'They shootin'!' vocal hits sit on downbeats; hook every 16 bars.

title: Paid In Full
structure: typical: 'Thinkin' of a master plan' opens the single verse over a sparse drum/bass loop, making it a long steady blend bed; famous spoken 'Pump up the volume' and other word hits land on downbeats.

title: Dirt Off Your Shoulder
structure: Tunebat lists 164 BPM, C-sharp major (3B); DJs count it half-time at 82. typical: synth riff intro with no vocal for the first phrase, hook 'get that dirt off your shoulder' every 16 bars; works as a half/double-time bridge into 160s trap or drum & bass.

title: HUMBLE.
structure: typical: 'Nobody pray for me' spoken intro then the piano riff drops with the beat; 'Sit down, be humble' hook is the drop-mix point; half-time at 75 bridges into 90s hip-hop when pitched.

title: Hypnotize
structure: typical: bass-line intro, first verse follows after one phrase, sung 'Biggie Biggie Biggie, can't you see' hook every 16 bars; the 'Uh' ad-libs are clean vocal hits.

title: In Da Club
mix: Album Version (Get Rich or Die Tryin')
structure: Sources list 89-90 BPM, C-sharp minor (12A); one mirror gives F-sharp minor (11A). typical: the string/synth riff intro runs clean before 'Go shorty, it's your birthday', which opens with the hook rather than a verse, so the hook is available as a drop-in from the top; hook returns every 16 bars.

title: Jump Around
structure: typical: horn-stab intro, the squeal sample hits on beat 1 of the hook, 'Jump around' chant every 16 bars; horn stab and squeal are the classic hot-cue hits.

artist: Fatman Scoop feat. The Crooklyn Clan
title: Be Faithful
structure: typical: party-rocking call-and-response record, shouted 'You got a hundred dollar bill, put your hands up' hooks every 8 bars over the 'Love Like This' loop; individual shouts are word hits for word-play drills.

title: Amen, Brother
structure: Documented: the Amen break is a four-bar drum solo by Gregory Coleman at 1:26, lasting about seven seconds; bars 1-2 repeat the previous groove, bar 3 delays a snare, bar 4 leaves beat 1 empty with a syncopated pattern and early crash. Use those four bars for juggling.

title: Apache
structure: Documented: an uncommonly long bongo/conga percussion break in the middle of the song is what Kool Herc looped with two copies ('merry-go-round'). Exact timestamp not stated by source. typical: the break is the drum/bongo-only passage after the second melody statement.

title: Funky Drummer
structure: Documented: the eight-bar, roughly 20-second Clyde Stubblefield drum break sits at 5:34 on the full-length version, with Brown's 'Ain't it funky?' spoken four times over it. The rest is a loosely arranged jam, so only the break is phrase-stable.

title: Think (About It)
structure: Single version listed at 113-114 BPM, A major (11B); Tunebat's full-length entry instead lists 126 BPM, F-sharp minor (11A), so confirm before relying on tempo. typical: the 'Yeah! Woo!' drum-and-shout break (the 'It Takes Two' sample) sits mid-song; the shouts land on downbeats for word play.

title: Nautilus
structure: typical: sparse drum-and-bass intro before the Fender Rhodes enters, so the opening bars are a clean blend bed; the Rhodes stabs are hot-cue hits.

title: Impeach The President
structure: Documented: the drum break opens the record (the beat that opens the song, with the hi-hat lifted near the end of the pattern), so the break is at the very top; Marley Marl looped it for MC Shan's 'The Bridge' in 1986.

title: Change The Beat
structure: Beatport lists 97 BPM, D minor (7A); Side A runs 7:37 with Fab 5 Freddy rapping in English and French. Documented: the vocoder tag 'Ahhh, this stuff is really fresh!' closes the Beside (B-side, Ann Boyle) version and is one of the most-sampled scratch sounds ever. Exact timestamp not stated by source.

title: Superseal 6
structure: Discogs states Side A is for scratching electro and half-tempo beats at 133 BPM (with a bonus drum-scratching section), Side B for mid-tempo beats at 100 BPM. No musical key (atonal scratch samples). Skipless: each locked groove repeats the same sample every rotation.

title: Battle Breaks
structure: Documented: first released as a 12" in 1992 and described as the first record made specifically for scratch battle DJs; the 7" reissue is BB001. BPM is nominal: source does not state a tempo, and skipless battle loops at 33 rpm are commonly cut at 100 or 133.33 BPM. No musical key.

title: Scratch Sounds No.2 (Reggae Clash)
structure: Discogs states 28 skip-proof scratch phrases, side one programmed at 83.33 BPM and side two at 100 BPM. No musical key. Release year not confirmed from source.

title: Super Seal Giant Robo V.1 (Head)
structure: Discogs states one side has skipless samples for half-time and fast beats (66 / 133 BPM) and the other side skipless samples for funky mid-tempo at 100 BPM; part of a seven-record Giant Robo set. No musical key.

title: Gypsy Woman (She's Homeless)
structure: typical: 'La da dee, la da da' hook is an isolated vocal phrase that lands on the downbeat, ideal for word-play; organ riff intro runs one phrase before the vocal.

title: Finally
structure: typical: piano-vamp intro with no vocal for the first phrase, 'Finally, it has happened to me' hook every 16 bars; the 12" Choice Mix carries the club arrangement and an acapella circulates widely.

title: It's Not Right But It's Okay
structure: typical: long drum/filtered intro before the vocal; the 'It's not right, but it's okay' hook is a clean 8-bar drop and 'Uh-huh' ad-libs are word hits on downbeats.

title: 24K Magic
structure: Tunebat mirrors list 107 BPM, D-flat major (3B); some other analyzers give F minor (4A, the relative minor). typical: talk-box 'Tonight, I just want to take you higher' intro phrase before the drums drop, hook 'Twenty-four karat magic in the air' every 16 bars; the drum drop is the drop-mix point.

title: Don't Start Now
structure: typical: bass-and-vocal intro from bar 1, pre-chorus build then 'Don't show up, don't come out' hook every 16 bars; the string stabs are hot-cue hits and 124 makes it a house-tempo bridge.

title: Crazy In Love
structure: typical: the Chi-Lites horn riff opens with no drums for the first phrase, 'Uh oh, uh oh' vocal hits sit on the downbeat, hook every 16 bars; the horn stab is the standard hot-cue hit and the JAY-Z verse is a clean 16 for blend-outs.

title: Don't Stop The Music
structure: typical: 'Please don't stop the music' spoken intro before the beat, 'Mama-say mama-sa' Michael Jackson chant is an isolated vocal hook on the downbeat; steady four-on-the-floor makes it the house-to-pop transition staple.
